statusNote: Third revision of this receipt. The r5 confirmation run compiled and executed the current test source (sha256 eeda0b26..., 857 lines, 10 tests) under the same three-suite filter: 92 cases, 91 passed, 1 failed, zero compile aborts. That one failure is the same pre-existing defect recorded in failedOrUnRun. This revision adds the three items the P1 review asked for: continuityToleranceTable (an explicit numeric tolerance table), builderProvenance (metadata labels proving the owner Editor builder generated the scene and geometry under test), and an ObservedFrame invariance section plus new assertions in the C# source (aliasing probes and a third coexisting carriage pose). The previous revision's status string stays in statusHistory.
title: [FMP-08a] rail alignment, moving carriage frame, boarding/alighting continuity
scopeStatement: Coordinate-continuity contract for the synthetic design table foundation/world/connected-world-profile.json. Surveyed rail alignment, real carriage envelope, real platform edge, operator acceptance and the 20 Hz whole-server frame budget were neither supplied nor measured: all NOT_ASSESSED. 'Alignment' here is an authored synthetic frame origin/yaw, not a survey, and must not be cited as surveyed alignment evidence.
perAssertionDetail: Per-assertion rationale and tolerances live in the submitted test source (ChooGuard.Foundation.Multiplayer.Tests, NUnit EditMode). This file is the receipt, the numeric summary, and the explicit tolerance table below.

fixture.derivation: ConnectedWorldSceneBuilder.Build emitted a bootstrap plus 13 region scenes; the test opens them additively, captures supports and the boarding bridge from real Unity colliders via ConnectedWorldGeometry.Capture, then re-reads the profile with JsonUtility and compares it byte-for-byte with the regenerated profile.
fixture.bodyRosterNote: Each test's adapter adds only its own body: one carriage, one boarding portal. The rebinding planes 12.5 +/- (0.3 + 0.035) depend on this radius and must be recomputed for any other.
fixture.definitionHashNote: Synthetic constant filling WorldState.SimulationDefinitionHash in the fixture; not a hash of any file.

continuityToleranceTable.note: The explicit numeric table the P1 review asked for. Every row is an assertion that exists in Fmp08aMovingFrameTests.cs at the cited line; 'assertedBy' is the test that owns it, so each row can be re-checked by reading that test at that line. 'kind' is 'exact' when the assertion is bit-equality (NUnit Is.Zero or an exact Equals on an integer/tick) and 'window' when it is an inequality or a +/- literal. No value here was measured by a separate instrument: they are the tolerances the definition and the movement contract are pinned to, and the tests are the authority. 0 m values are exact-equality assertions on float distance-squared, not measurements with a resolution.

alignmentTolerance.yaw: SimulatedSpatialWorld.TrainAligned(:93-96) accepts a carriage as aligned only when origin distance squared <= .0025 and YawDegrees and Origin.Y exactly equal the authored values; 0.05 m / 0 degrees / identical Y are the synthetic contract values. See continuityToleranceTable CF-09/CF-10/CF-11.
alignmentTolerance.note: YawIsHalfOfTheAlignmentToleranceAndTheMetroFrameRoundTripsAt180Degrees perturbs the yaw term and the Y term separately and demands rejection, because tests that only move the distance still pass if the yaw term disappears.

alignmentBeforeAfter.builderRegeneration: The generated profile text was byte-identical to foundation/world/connected-world-profile.json (14 region scene paths).
alignmentBeforeAfter.pinned: After alignment the carriage frame origin is exactly (-37.5, 2, 15), yaw 0, Y unchanged, and non-carriage frames move zero. The pinned body keeps LocalPosition (0,0,0) with Position.X == -37.5 and Position == frame.ToWorld(LocalPosition): moving the carriage 12.5 m leaves the carriage-local pose unchanged and only the world pose follows, through the same transform.

transformContinuity.pinned: In the single tick that moves the carriage frame 4 m, the Unity transforms of the boarding bridge and platform floor did not move within 1e-6 (the bridge is station geometry in the world frame) while the carriage floor moved +4 m. The platform body stayed fixed within 1e-9, its support stayed floor.rail_platforms_mainline and the contact space stayed world.

pinnedBodyFollowsCarriage.pinned: Each tick the carriage body's world X gain equals that tick's frame delta within 1e-4, even across the 0.44/0.5 m step, so it moves by exactly the delta and never jumps. Each tick the carriage-local LocalPosition is unchanged within 1e-9, the platform body stays fixed within 1e-9 and its support is unchanged, and the contact space goes from world on the first tick to train-mainline on the last.

boundaryCrossing.pinned: Each tick the carriage body's world X displacement equals the offset within 5e-5, so there is no jump at the boundary. The contact space is 'world' at 0.02/0.04/0.0499 and 'train-mainline' at 0.0501/0.06/0.08: it flips exactly on either side of the tolerance (distance squared .0025 = 0.05 m). Per-tick displacement equals the difference from the previous offset within 1e-4, so the flip adds no displacement; FrameId stays train-mainline throughout with LocalPosition (0,0,0).

directionsCovered: boarding: platform -> fixed bridge -> carriage floor (station arm of TryLocate)
alighting: carriage floor -> fixed bridge -> platform floor (carriage arm of TryLocate, decision at SimulatedSpatialWorld.cs:65)
boardingAndAlighting.pinned: The support sequence is exactly {platform floor, fixed bridge, carriage floor} for boarding and the exact reverse for alighting, and no other support ever appears: the walk never steps directly between platform floor and carriage floor in either direction. There are exactly two support handovers per direction, at the authored planes Z = 5.0 (station-side) and Z = 12.5 (doorway) within 0.25 m; the frame changes exactly once per direction and never flips back. The support handover tick precedes the frame handover tick, and every per-tick displacement is under 0.25 m, so no frame-sized jump occurs anywhere in the walk.
boardingAndAlighting.pinnedAlighting: The carriage-to-station rebinding happens at Z = 12.5 - 0.3 - 0.035 = 12.165 m, clear of the doorway. Across every on-bridge tick, the maximum world Z of ticks that keep the carriage frame is at least 12.165 - .01 and the maximum world Z of ticks that switched to the world frame is below 12.165 + .01; the flip tick is the tick immediately after the last carriage-frame bridge tick (compared by tick number). On the bridge the world Z decreases monotonically toward 5.0, passing 12.835 -> 12.5 -> 5.0 in order, with carriage coordinates still in force at 12.835 and 12.5 and world coordinates already in force at 5.0, and every per-tick world displacement is under 0.25 m. Repeating the walk with the carriage frame moved -0.048 m in Z (inside the tolerance) asserts the carriage-floor support's turnover plane follows the live frame delta, not an authored constant.
boardingAndAlighting.pinnedStationSide: A body on the bridge stays in the world frame and keeps its PortalId, with BoardingOccupied = true and CanClosePortal = false; departure (TryApplyFrames) then fails with 'Occupied portal prevents closure/departure', and ExportCheckpoint() is byte-identical before and after the failure, so there is no partial commit. Even after the refused departure, a body that clears the bridge reaches the carriage floor and the carriage frame. The carriage floor is never claimed before the authored doorway Z = 12.5, the carriage floor binds before the frame, and after the transition the carriage-local LocalPosition matches the carriage frame's world coordinates within 1e-7.
boardingAndAlighting.branchExecuted: CarriageToPlatformAlightingStepsThroughTheStationBridgeOnce genuinely traverses the carriage-local guard at SimulatedSpatialWorld.TryLocate(:60) and the rebinding decision inside it (:65). (1) It locates those two lines by string equality rather than line number, asserting the guard exists and the decision is the fifth statement inside it, so it cannot pass if the branch is moved or deleted. (2) It asserts an observation only that branch can produce: on the bridge there are both ticks that keep the carriage frame and ticks that switched to the world frame, their boundary being exactly the footprint-clearance plane 12.165. Separately, for the same prior carriage pose it asserts directly that world Z 12.30 resolves to the carriage and 12.10 to the station (12.10 lies outside the platform region, so that station pose cannot come from ordinary containment).
boardingAndAlighting.note: The support-surface-confusion negative case was made concrete as (a) a direct platform-floor to carriage-floor transition, (b) inversion of support and frame ordering, (c) claiming the carriage floor in front of the doorway, (d) rebinding a bridge body to the departing carriage frame; each is blocked by its own assertion. The earlier revision that walked boarding only is not presented as boarding/alighting coverage: this revision added the alighting walk as a separate test, which is the basis of branchExecuted above.

historicalReportPose.pinned: Stored report-1 has ObservedFrame.Origin equal to the observation-time authored origin (-50,2,15) and ObservedSimulationTick 0. After the carriage moves 42 m, report-1's ObservedFrame.Origin is still (-50,2,15) and is not equal to the post-move origin, confirming in both directions that the current carriage pose did not overwrite it (Position and LocalPosition are likewise the observation-time values). A newly issued report-2 captures the post-move carriage pose and tick 1 and does not rewrite report-1. Replaying all sink commits through the approved Replay restores report-1 to the authored origin and report-2 to the post-move origin, with the current frame at the post-move origin. ValidReportPose is checked against the frozen report.ObservedFrame, never the live frame (AuthoritativeShift.cs:383-390).

observedFrameInvariance.statement: ObservedFrame is never overwritten by the current carriage pose, and it is never an alias of a live frame object. The report snapshot is taken once, at commit time, as a copy (AuthoritativeShift.cs:220), and nothing in the test can reach it through the live state.

aliasingProbes.probe: two successive ExportCheckpoint() calls must return distinct ObservedFrame instances (line 545)
aliasingProbes.catches: TeamReport.Copy() dropping its ObservedFrame copy; a report that aliases the checkpoint it was read through
aliasingProbes.wouldNotCatch: an alias between the stored report and the shift's internal state frame when nothing in the test holds a reference to that state frame

aliasingProbes.probe: ReadSimulation() must return frames distinct from the caller's array, and clobbering one must not move the live frame (lines 556-559)

observedFrameInvariance.honestLimitation: AuthoritativeShift keeps its own copies at every boundary this test can observe (constructor :31, ApplyServerSimulationCore :91, ExportCheckpoint :43, ReadSimulation :47), so the test has no handle on the internal state frame object. The probes above therefore catch a missing copy at the report and view boundaries, which is where the mutation-free code path is reachable; they cannot directly catch a hypothetical report that aliased the internal state frame, because that object is not exposed. The value-freeze assertions (RP-01 to RP-05, RP-08, RP-09) are what pin the observable behaviour regardless.

historicalReportPose.note: The old-report-overwritten negative case is checked at seven moments, M1-M7 above.

mutationRun.interpretation: The mutation broke exactly the assertions it targeted. The two boarding/alighting tests do not move the carriage frame through the adapter during the walk, so the delta correction is a no-op for them and they do not verify it; that claim rests on the four failing tests above. The new provenance test does not use the adapter at all and the report test drives AuthoritativeShift rather than the adapter, so neither is expected to catch this mutation: their 6/6 pass under mutation is a statement about their scope, not about the mutation.
mutationRun.windowCaveat: One shared working tree: the mutation existed only for the run and was reverted immediately, but a run started by another item in that window could have seen the mutated assembly. The window was kept minimal by narrowing the filter to this work item's 10 cases (3.0 s of test time) and reverting as the next command after the run reported completion.
mutationRun.revert: After reverting, the sha256 matched pristineSha256, and git status showed no changes under Runtime/ or Multiplayer/Runtime/.
